correctness.rationale: PASS: Each order-five binary de Bruijn cycle has exactly 32 distinct cyclic length-five windows; a marked position belongs to five of them, so every circular string attractor has at least ceil(32/5)=7 positions. Each cyclic word corresponds uniquely to a 32-vertex Hamilton tour of overlapping five-bit windows rooted at the unique 00000 occurrence; exact DFS counts 2048 such words. A seven-position set hits all unique length-five windows iff all cyclic intermarked gaps are at most five, giving exactly 384 candidates independent of the cycle. Those selected length-five incidences automatically hit any factor of length >=5; for lengths 1..4 the union-of-all-occurrence position masks supply necessary-and-sufficient tests. Independently implemented C++ reconstruction exhausted 2048 tours ×384 complete candidate sets, reproducing minimum 216 (4 words), maximum 368 (2 words), 120 distinct counts, and total 589120. Its deterministically sorted complete 2048-row CSV SHA-256 is 8bb608eb66f3bfac0152475146822a21df2a5ecb9665f2f9193ef22ec4291ea2, exactly matching frozen census.csv. Direct proof of exhaustive object/candidate parametrization converts finite enumeration to an exact finite theorem; no infinite claim made.
residual_risks: Exact only for binary order-five cyclic de Bruijn words, all 2048 rotation classes; not a theorem for other orders or larger alphabets.
Machine calculations corroborate only stated finite domains; all-degree/all-prime claims depend on mathematical proofs.

Full optimizer multiplicity census of a canonical closed finite family supplies useful optimality/rigidity data not determined by just one benchmark word or the optimum size.
